facts.text: Mark Leonard stopped writing annual President letters in 2018. He stated this was because the rest of the world caught on to Constellation's playbook, and sharing their hard-won tactics with competitors simply was not in the best interest of long-term shareholders.

At the time of initial public offering (early 2000s), Constellation Software established an objective of generating in excess of 20% average annual revenue growth per share and EBITDA growth per share for the period January 1, 2006 through December 31, 2010.
facts.source_title: Issuu - Mark Leonard Extraordinary CEO 2021 Letter

facts.text: On September 25, 2025, Constellation Software announced that Mark Leonard resigned as President for health reasons, effective immediately. Mark Miller, the Chief Operating Officer, was appointed as the new President by the Board of Directors.
facts.source_title: Constellation Software - Mark Leonard Resignation & Mark Miller Appointment

facts.text: On March 27, 2026, Constellation announced that Mark Leonard would not stand for re-election to the Board of Directors. However, Leonard continued to serve as an advisor to Constellation, focusing on supporting the company's Permanent Engaged Minority Shareholder (PEMS) strategy.
facts.source_title: Yahoo Finance - Mark Leonard Board Departure

facts.text: Organic growth has been flat to negative in recent periods relative to the 4% FX-adjusted growth (excluding US Healthcare) achieved in 2015-2018. This reflects the company's shift to acquisition-driven growth as a primary strategy.
facts.source_title: Eagle Point Capital - Constellation Software Anti-Conglomerate

facts.text: In his 2021 letter, Mark Leonard said Constellation would stop paying special dividends and reinvest its free cash flow, even if that meant pursuing larger acquisitions at lower expected rates of return and moving into new industries, because he believed CSI could invest capital more effectively than most of its shareholders could on their own.

Leonard's letter reasoning: historically CSI targeted roughly 30% ROIC on acquisitions, but a single larger acquisition earning only 20% ROIC on $600 million of capital would generate as much annual cash as eight separate $50 million acquisitions at the higher hurdle rate -- an argument for lowering the hurdle rate to deploy more capital into bigger deals.

Third-party research describes a tiered IRR hurdle rate at CSI: approximately 30% for acquisitions under $1 million of revenue, 20% for those over $4 million, and 25% in between. The same research states CSI has changed its overall hurdle rate three times in twenty years (one increase, two decreases), and that lowering it dragged down the expected IRR of the whole subsequent acquisition pipeline.
facts.source_title: Hurdle Rate Discipline Is a Core Strength of Constellation's Acquisition Strategy | Morningstar

facts.text: On November 17, 2020, Constellation Software provided an update on a previously declared conditional special dividend connected to the proposed Topicus.com spin-out, indicating the dividend was contingent on conditions tied to the spin-out.
facts.source_title: Constellation Software Inc Provides Update in Connection with Proposed Topicus.com Spin Out and Previously Declared Conditional Dividend

facts.text: Constellation Software's leadership treats 'ROIC + organic growth' as the core measure of capital allocation effectiveness: the cash return earned on invested capital added to the rate at which existing businesses grow on their own, treated as the annual increase in intrinsic shareholder value. One letter states: 'Achieving even 24% ROIC+OGr is non-trivial. We believe that less than 10% of public companies have been able to achieve this level of performance for an extended period.'
